Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which statement about the behaviour of firms in a planned economy is correct?

options.A: Firms are sent signals to produce through the price mechanism.
options.B: Firms will operate in competitive markets.
options.C: Firms will attempt to make profits for the benefit of shareholders.
options.D: Firms are more likely to consider the private and external costs of production.

questions.questionText: The table provides information on entrepreneurship among males in three countries in 2013. percentage of males percentage of males with access to with access to training on how to finance to start start a business (%) a business (%) Italy 19.1 10.3 Japan 31.3 34.0 Sweden 61.6 49.7 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: In Sweden, it is easier for male entrepreneurs to get training than finance.
options.B: It is always more difficult for male entrepreneurs to get finance than training.
options.C: Italy provides less money for male entrepreneurs than Japan or Sweden.
options.D: Sweden has more male entrepreneurs than Italy or Japan.

questions.questionText: What can be measured by cross-elasticity of demand?

options.A: a change in real income as a result of a change in the price of consumer goods
options.B: a change in the demand for a good in response to a change in the price of a complement
options.C: a change in the price of a good in response to a change in the demand for a substitute
options.D: a change in the price of a good when the demand for it changes

questions.questionText: The table shows the maximum price a consumer would be willing to pay for successive cans of fruit juice. cans first second third fourth fifth price ($) 14 10 6 4 3 The price of a can of fruit juice is $4 and, having bought three cans, the consumer decides to buy a fourth. How does buying the fourth can affect his consumer surplus?

options.A: It leaves it unchanged.
options.B: It lowers it by $2.
options.C: It raises it by $4.
options.D: It raises it by $34.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows four supply curves.
The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for a good in a free market. S price P D O Q quantity What can definitely be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: All the costs and benefits of consumption are reflected in OP .
options.B: At OP consumer expenditure is greater than the firm’s revenue.
options.C: At OP the price elasticity of supply is equal to one.
options.D: The market will not clear at a price of OP .

questions.questionText: The demand for a good increases. Under which circumstances will the quantity supplied of the good rise the most?

options.A: It is an agricultural good that has an annual growing cycle and requires a cool climate.
options.B: It is an agricultural good that is perishable and very expensive to store.
options.C: It is a manufactured good that uses unskilled labour and there is unemployment in the economy.
options.D: It is a manufactured good that uses capital-intensive production and it is currently at full capacity.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve and supply curve for a good on which the government imposes a specific tax. S price D D S O quantity What will be the result of this tax?

options.A: Most of the incidence of the tax will fall on the producer.
options.B: There will be a new demand curve parallel to DD.
options.C: The price will rise by the full amount of the tax.
options.D: The quantity bought will fall proportionately to the tax rate.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows how a 10% increase in consumer incomes shifts the demand for good X from

options.D: It is an inferior good with income inelastic demand.
options.A: It is a normal good with income elastic demand.
options.B: It is a normal good with income inelastic demand.
options.C: It is an inferior good with income elastic demand.

questions.questionText: What is an example of privatisation?

options.A: the sale on the market of a French state-owned power-generation company
options.B: the sale of a privately-owned water company to a German firm
options.C: the takeover of a French car manufacturer by the French government
options.D: the purchase of a Swedish pharmaceutical producer by a larger American pharmaceutical producer

questions.questionText: What did Adam Smith mean by ‘economy’ when describing his canons of taxation?

options.A: The cost of collecting the tax should be low.
options.B: The tax should be easy to pay.
options.C: The tax should have a neutral effect on the use of resources.
options.D: The tax should have a positive effect on aggregate supply.

questions.questionText: A government decides to remove fees for higher education provided by the public sector and the private sector. What is the consequence of this policy?

options.A: Higher education is less likely to be provided by the private sector.
options.B: Resources in higher education will be allocated through the price mechanism.
options.C: The demand for higher education will be perfectly elastic when the price is zero.
options.D: The opportunity cost of higher education to students will be zero.

questions.questionText: What would be the main effect of imposing an effective maximum price on foodstuffs?

options.A: Inflation would rise.
options.B: The price of foodstuffs would rise.
options.C: There would be a decrease in the import of foodstuffs.
options.D: There would be a shortage of foodstuffs.

questions.questionText: An effective minimum price is applied to alcohol in an attempt to reduce consumption. Why would a government not buy up any surplus created?

options.A: Buying the surplus would be costly to the government.
options.B: Buying the surplus would decrease the incomes of producers.
options.C: Buying the surplus would lead to a shortage.
options.D: Buying the surplus would lead to unemployment.

questions.questionText: A government plans to increase spending on education and training every year. Which diagram shows the likely effect of this increase on the economy’s long-run output and price level?

options.A: B LRAS LRAS LRAS

questions.questionText: What is disinflation?

options.A: a fall in output
options.B: a fall in the price level
options.C: a fall in the rate of increase of the price level
options.D: a fall in the value of national income

questions.questionText: What best describes a country’s terms of trade?

options.A: the difference between the volume of its exports and its imports
options.B: the average price of its exports divided by the average price of its imports
options.C: the total value of its exports divided by the total value of its imports
options.D: the volume of its exports divided by the volume of its imports

questions.questionText: A developed country has a price-inelastic demand for oil, all of which it imports. The oil-producing countries increase the supply of oil. What is likely to happen to the developed country’s rate of inflation and its balance of trade? rate of inflation balance of trade

options.A: decreases improves
options.B: decreases worsens
options.C: increases improves
options.D: increases worsens

questions.questionText: Country X and country Y both produce rice and tables. Half of their resources are used to produce rice and the other half to produce tables. The resulting output of each product is given in the table shown. country rice tables X 150 100 Y 100 50 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Country X has a comparative advantage in the production of both goods.
options.B: Country X has a comparative advantage in the production of rice.
options.C: Country Y has a comparative advantage in the production of both goods.
options.D: Country Y has a comparative advantage in the production of rice.

questions.questionText: An economy experiences a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. What could the economy do to finance this deficit?

options.A: adopt a fixed exchange rate
options.B: attract more foreign direct investment
options.C: decrease income tax rates
options.D: lower the rate of interest

questions.questionText: A resident of country X buys shares in a firm in country Y. The shares then pay the resident a dividend. Where are these two flows recorded in country X’s balance of payments? purchase dividend

options.A: capital account primary income (income)
options.B: capital account secondary income (current transfers)
options.C: financial account primary income (income)
options.D: financial account secondary income (current transfers)

questions.questionText: What is the most likely cause of cost-push inflation in an economy?

options.A: an increase in the exchange rate
options.B: an increase in the money supply
options.C: an increase in the prices of imports
options.D: an increase in the rate of income tax

questions.questionText: Which changes are most likely to reduce the accuracy of the consumer prices index (CPI) as a measurement of inflation?

options.A: A larger sample is used in the household spending survey.
options.B: Technology makes it easier for retailers to submit accurate monthly price data.
options.C: Households change their spending habits.
options.D: The weightings attached to the basket of goods are reviewed more often.

questions.questionText: A government reduces the rate of direct income tax and devalues its currency. Which row describes the policy effects of these decisions? fiscal policy monetary policy supply-side policy

options.A: contractionary expansionary contractionary
options.B: expansionary contractionary expansionary
options.C: expansionary expansionary contractionary
options.D: expansionary expansionary expansionary

questions.questionText: The balance of payments on the current account for Guatemala in 2011 was –US$1.6bn and in 2016 was +US$1.0bn. What is most likely to have been a contributory factor to this change in the balance of payments on the current account over this five-year period?

options.A: an appreciation of Guatemala’s currency
options.B: a growth of household incomes in Guatemala
options.C: a lowering of tariffs on goods imported into Guatemala
options.D: productivity improvements in Guatemala’s export sector

questions.questionText: The government wishes to increase aggregate demand. Which actions would be most likely to succeed?

options.A: a reduction in income tax and an increase in interest rates
options.B: a reduction in income tax and an increase in production subsidies
options.C: an increase in corporate tax and an increase in government spending
